preserved_objections.basis: The candidate's mechanism relies on altering crystallization kinetics of CaCO3 and CaSO4•2H2O through electromagnetic fields, but the provided evidence (doi:10.1038/s41545-026-00565-8) only provides temporal insights into the scaling pathways, not the actual effect of electromagnetic fields on crystallization kinetics.

The candidate's intervention is only tested on a specific type of brackish-water reverse-osmosis desalination skid, but the provided evidence (doi:10.1016/s0011-9164(00)88638-5) shows that reverse osmosis can be applied to both brackish and seawater, indicating that the boundary conditions may not be well-defined.

The candidate's predicted effect (maintaining normalized permeate flux above 85% for 12 months) is equivalent to the baseline (current brackish-water reverse-osmosis desalination skid), as the provided evidence (doi:10.1016/j.desal.2012.02.024) shows that optimal plant operation can maintain flux above 85% for 12 months without any intervention.
